Name: Lisa Pruett
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Looking back on this inquiry cycle, I learned that my students are far more engaged and thoughtful than their written work alone often shows. Through strategies like visual-based They Say / I Say and structured routines, I noticed that students had clear opinions and strong reasoning when they were given accessible entry points and time to talk before writing. This helped me realize that reluctance to write was not a lack of understanding, but often a lack of confidence or support in how to begin.

What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

Coming out of this module, I’m left with new questions about how to gradually release scaffolds without losing student engagement. I’m curious about when and how to fade sentence frames, visuals, and structured routines so students can transfer these skills to more independent writing tasks. I also wonder how these strategies might impact students’ stamina and quality of writing over a longer period of time.
